# terraform-provider-developer knowledge log

This is the reinforcement log for the vendor-agnostic base agent
([terraform-provider-developer.agent.md](terraform-provider-developer.agent.md)).
It is **append-only** - never rewrite or delete a prior entry, only add new
ones below. Only genuinely vendor-agnostic findings belong here (a codegen
toolchain quirk, a generic hand-written-CRUD pattern, a portability fix, an
agent/prompt authoring convention). Vendor-specific findings (SDK type
shapes, API behavior, tenant-specific quirks) belong in the relevant vendor
specialist's own knowledge file instead - if you're not sure which file an
entry belongs in, ask: "would this be true for a completely different
vendor's OpenAPI-codegen-based Terraform provider?" If yes, it belongs here.

## Entry Template

```
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Task type: pipeline | author-agent | review
- Target/Scope: <files touched or pipeline stage under discussion>
- Summary: <what was done/found, and why - cite evidence (command output,
  file/line) rather than asserting from memory>
- Delegated to: <specialist agent(s) invoked, or "none">
- Validation: <commands run and outcomes, Phase A / Phase B split if relevant>
- Guardrail update: <new Workflow/Enforcement Rule added, or "none">
```

- Date: 2026-07-28
- Task type: review
- Target/Scope: `terraform-provider-developer.agent.md` - stage 6 ("Hand-write CRUD") pattern catalog, and the "Prefer generation/config over repeated dynamic derivation" section.
- Summary: Generalized two hand-written-CRUD patterns first discovered on the IdentityNow specialist's `governance_group` target (members/connections sub-resources) into this vendor-agnostic base file, since both are genuinely toolchain/vendor-independent shapes rather than IdentityNow-specific quirks. (1) **"Join"/membership sub-resource with no single-item CRUD**: a parent-owned collection sub-endpoint shaped only as list+bulk-add+bulk-remove (no per-item get/patch/delete) does not fit the standard per-item CRUD codegen assumption; documented as its own hand-written resource pattern - own the complete desired set for one parent (parent id `Required`+`RequiresReplace`, a set-valued member-ids attribute `Required`), diff current-vs-desired on Create/Update and call bulk-add/bulk-remove only for deltas (treating per-item "already satisfied" errors as non-fatal), always re-list actual membership on Read (self-heal against out-of-band drift), and bulk-remove all tracked members on Delete (treating a 404 on the parent itself as a no-op) - analogous to `aws_iam_group_membership`-style resources elsewhere. (2) **Read-only sub-resource with no write endpoint at all**: a related collection that is entirely derived from the parent (membership established from the *other* object's configuration, not this one) has nothing to manage, so model it as a plain hand-written data source (no generated counterpart - there's no single-item CRUD shape to generate from) rather than a resource; don't assume its list endpoint shares the same max page size as the parent's own list endpoint - confirm independently. Also extended the existing "reusable script over one-off edit" principle's parenthetical example to explicitly cover required-ness/schema-shape corrections (not just type-mapping/renames) for a field the live API treats as required despite the spec's own `required` array omitting it - generalizing IdentityNow's `apply_codespec_schema_overrides.py` companion to the existing `apply_codespec_type_mappings.py` script.
- Delegated to: none (agent-file authoring/review pass, done directly).
- Validation: confirmed YAML front matter still parses (`python3`+`yaml.safe_load`, keys unchanged: `name`, `description`, `argument-hint`, `tools`, `user-invocable`); confirmed no vendor-specific facts (no SailPoint/IdentityNow/SDK-specific names) leaked into the new base-agent text - both new bullets are phrased purely in terms of generic OpenAPI/Terraform-framework concepts (parent id, member-id set, bulk-add/bulk-remove, list endpoint) with the `aws_iam_group_membership` reference used only as a cross-ecosystem analogy, not a dependency.
- Guardrail update: added two new recognized hand-written-CRUD patterns to stage 6 of the Generic Codegen Pipeline section (join/membership sub-resource; read-only no-write sub-resource data source), and broadened the schema-shape-override example in "Prefer generation/config over repeated dynamic derivation".

- Date: 2026-07-29
- Task type: review
- Target/Scope: `terraform-provider-developer.agent.md` - stage 6 ("Hand-write CRUD") JSON-Patch-update guidance bullet.
- Summary: Generalized two more vendor-agnostic hand-written-CRUD lessons discovered on the IdentityNow specialist's `sources` target while live-testing optional-field examples, both distinct from the already-documented "Join"/"Read-only sub-resource" patterns. (1) **"Read-back enrichment" pattern**: when a vendor API merges extra server/connector-managed keys into a JSON-blob-shaped attribute beyond what the practitioner configured, `dtoToModel`/its equivalent should preserve the practitioner's exact configured value when known/configured, only falling back to the full API-returned value when Null/Unknown (e.g. post-import) - otherwise every `plan`/`apply` shows permanent phantom drift from the server's injected keys. (2) A direct corollary for `Update`: once state deliberately preserves only the practitioner's narrower configured value (per pattern 1), a shared "unconditional replace op per attribute on every Update" JSON-Patch convention (already documented in this same bullet) must NOT be applied unconditionally to that specific attribute - only include its patch op when the plan's value actually differs from the last-read state's value. Confirmed live: including it unconditionally re-sent only the narrower configured subset on every update (even ones touching unrelated attributes), which one real API rejected with a confusing, seemingly-unrelated validation error blamed on a completely different, untouched, computed-only field - purely because the enriched attribute's shape changed relative to its true live value.
- Delegated to: none (agent-file authoring/review pass, done directly).
- Validation: confirmed YAML front matter still parses; confirmed the new text is phrased purely in generic terms (JSON-blob attribute, server-managed keys, patch op, plan-vs-state diff) with no SailPoint/IdentityNow-specific names.
- Guardrail update: extended stage 6's existing JSON-Patch-update bullet with the unconditional-patch pitfall, and added a new "Read-back enrichment" bullet documenting the corresponding `dtoToModel`-side half of the same pattern.

- Date: 2026-07-31
- Task type: review
- Target/Scope: `terraform-provider-developer.agent.md` (stage 6 hand-written-CRUD pattern catalog, Offline vs. Live Validation Phase B bullets, Enforcement Rules), `identitynow-terraform-provider-developer.agent.md` (test/README.md references repointed to docs/TESTING.md), root `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (Key conventions list, manual test config pointer).
- Summary: Promoted several genuinely vendor-agnostic lessons discovered during the IdentityNow specialist's `identity_v1`/`segment_access_v1`/`application_access_association_v1`/`entitlement_request_config_v1` live-testing pass (see the identitynow specialist's 2026-07-31 knowledge entry for full IdentityNow-specific detail) into this base file, generalized to remove all vendor-specific names:
  1. **"Distributed" membership resource pattern** (new stage-6 bullet): a variant of the existing "Join"/membership-sub-resource pattern for when there is no dedicated collection endpoint at all - membership instead lives as a scattered attribute on N separate parent objects (possibly of different types), each independently gettable/patchable. Same complete-desired-set ownership semantics as "Join", but implemented as an N-calls-per-apply GET+patch-preserving-others loop per member instead of one bulk endpoint.
  2. **Non-exclusive/partial association resource pattern** (new stage-6 bullet): distinct from "Join"'s exclusive full-membership ownership - some associations should only ever add/remove members *this resource instance* itself configured, always preserving anything else already attached by other means. Union-merge on Create, own-tracked-ids-only add/remove on Update, own-tracked-ids-only removal on Delete. Named the AWS analogy pair (`aws_iam_user_policy_attachment` non-exclusive vs. `aws_iam_group_membership` exclusive) as a cross-ecosystem reference point.
  3. **Optional+Computed-with-no-PlanModifier Unknown-vs-Null gotcha** (new stage-6 bullet): a field with no `PlanModifier` reports Unknown (not Null) when a practitioner omits it from config, since the framework can't statically know if the provider computes a value. A conversion function checking only `IsNull()` is an incomplete guard for the normal case of an omitted Optional field - must check `!IsNull() && !IsUnknown()`, treating Unknown the same as Null when the field is purely practitioner-supplied.
  4. **Direct-API cross-verification requirement for association/sub-resource Phase B testing** (new Offline vs. Live Validation Phase B bullet): a clean `terraform plan`/successful `apply` is insufficient live verification for any resource managing an association rather than a fully-owned object lifecycle - Terraform's own state can look internally consistent while the underlying write path is completely non-functional (this is exactly how a fundamentally broken design based on a nonexistent API endpoint passed every check until a direct out-of-band API call caught it). Always issue a direct API call confirming the actual parent/foreign object's own field state at each CRUD step.
  5. Two Enforcement Rules already added mid-session (spec-file-presence-doesn't-prove-liveness; never-trust-a-delegated-agent's-self-report-without-re-running) were confirmed still present and correctly generalized - no further edit needed there this pass, just verified.
  Also repointed the IdentityNow specialist's two `test/README.md` references to `docs/TESTING.md` (created this session as the new canonical, git-tracked location for manual-test-config conventions, since `test/` itself must stay gitignored for credential reasons) and refreshed `copilot-instructions.md`'s own Key Conventions list and manual-test-config section to match.
- Delegated to: none (agent-file authoring/review pass, done directly by the primary session, not a background agent).
- Validation: confirmed YAML front matter still parses on all three edited files (`python3`+`yaml.safe_load` on the front-matter block); confirmed the new stage-6 bullets and Phase B bullet contain no vendor-specific names (SailPoint/IdentityNow/SDK-specific identifiers) - phrased purely in terms of generic OpenAPI/Terraform-framework concepts, with the AWS resource-name cross-references used only as ecosystem analogies, not dependencies; confirmed `docs/TESTING.md` exists and is git-trackable (`git check-ignore` returns non-zero) while `test/README.md` remains gitignored (`git check-ignore` returns zero, matches `test/` pattern) via direct check.
- Guardrail update: added 3 new hand-written-CRUD patterns to stage 6 (distributed membership; non-exclusive/partial association; Optional+Computed Unknown-vs-Null) and 1 new Phase B validation bullet (direct-API cross-verification for association resources) to `terraform-provider-developer.agent.md`.
